title: Z80A 8-bit microprocessor (4 MHz grade of the Z80 CPU), N-channel MOS

pins.name: INT
pins.text: interrupt request from I/O devices; honoured at the end of the current instruction if the interrupt enable flip-flop (IFF) is set; sampled at the rising clock edge of the last clock of an instruction

pins.name: NMI
pins.text: non-maskable interrupt: higher priority than INT, always recognised at the end of the current instruction whatever the IFF; forces a restart to 0066H)

pins.name: HALT
pins.text: low when the CPU has executed a HALT instruction and waits for an interrupt; while halted it executes NOPs to keep memory refresh going

pins.name: MREQ
pins.text: memory request: the address bus holds a valid address for a memory read or write

pins.name: IORQ
pins.text: input/output request: the lower half of the address bus holds a valid I/O address for an I/O read or write; also low together with M1 during interrupt acknowledge, so the device can put its vector on the data bus

pins.name: RD
pins.text: read: the CPU wants to read data from memory or an I/O device; the addressed device gates its data onto the bus

pins.name: WR
pins.text: write: the CPU data bus holds valid data to be stored in the addressed memory or I/O device

pins.name: BUSAK
pins.text: bus acknowledge: low when the address bus, data bus and tri-state control signals have been set to high impedance after a BUSRQ

pins.name: WAIT
pins.text: the addressed memory or I/O device is not ready; the CPU enters wait states for as long as it is low; set up 70 ns before the falling clock edge

pins.name: BUSRQ
pins.text: bus request (active low): higher priority than NMI, recognised at the end of the current machine cycle; the CPU then floats its address bus, data bus and tri-state control outputs and answers with BUSAK. Listed as an enable that is active while HIGH (no request) because the outputs drive only then.

pins.name: RESET
pins.text: resets the interrupt enable flip-flop, clears PC and registers I and R, sets interrupt mode 0 (8080A mode); during reset the address and data bus are high impedance and all control outputs inactive; must be low for at least 3 clock cycles

pins.name: M1
pins.text: machine cycle one: the current machine cycle is the op code fetch of an instruction; with IORQ it marks interrupt acknowledge

pins.name: RFSH
pins.text: refresh: the lower 7 bits of the address bus hold a refresh address for dynamic memories and the current MREQ should be used for a refresh read

pins.name: A0
pins.text: address bus bit 0 (least significant)

functions.text: 16-bit address bus: memory addresses (64K bytes) and, on A0-A7, I/O port addresses. During T3 and T4 of an op code fetch the lower 7 bits carry the refresh address (RFSH low). High impedance during reset and while the bus is granted (BUSAK low).

8-bit bidirectional data bus. Data is read at the rising clock edge of T3 of an op code fetch; for a write it is driven while WR is low. During interrupt acknowledge (M1 and IORQ low) the device puts an 8-bit vector on the bus.

Bus control: op code fetch = M1 low, address = PC, MREQ and RD low, then refresh in T3-T4 (RFSH and MREQ low, refresh address). Memory read/write = MREQ low with RD or WR low (three clock states). I/O read/write = IORQ low with RD or WR low; one wait state Tw* is added automatically. Interrupt acknowledge = a special M1 cycle with IORQ (not MREQ) low and two automatic wait states.

state.organisation: registers (208 bits of read/write storage): main set A, F, B, C, D, E, H, L; alternate set A', F', B', C', D', E', H', L'; special registers I (interrupt vector), R (memory refresh), IX, IY, SP, PC
state.changesOn: clock PHI; RESET low acts while held
rules: 158 instructions, including all 78 of the 8080A; the full table is on pages 4-5 of the source: 8-bit and 16-bit loads, exchanges (EX DE,HL; EX AF,AF'; EXX; EX (SP),ss), block moves LDI/LDIR/LDD/LDDR, block searches CPI/CPIR/CPD/CPDR, 8-bit ALU (ADD, ADC, SUB, SBC, AND, OR, XOR, CP, INC, DEC), 16-bit arithmetic, DAA, CPL, NEG, CCF, SCF, NOP, HALT, DI, EI, IM 0/1/2, rotates and shifts (RLC, RL, RRC, RR, SLA, SRA, SRL, RLD, RRD), BIT/SET/RES, I/O (IN, OUT, INI, INIR, IND, INDR, OUTI, OTIR, OUTD, OTDR), jumps (JP, JR, DJNZ), CALL, RST, RET, RETI, RETN.

Interrupt modes: IM 0 = 8080A mode; IM 1 = call to 0038H; IM 2 = indirect call: register I gives the upper 8 bits and the interrupting device the lower 8 bits of a pointer into a table of service addresses.
NMI: restart at 0066H, independent of the interrupt enable flip-flop.
RESET: IFF reset, PC = 0, I = 0, R = 0, interrupt mode 0.
R register: the lower 7 bits are put on the address bus during refresh; the refresh is automatic and transparent.

electrical.notes: Z80A D.C. characteristics (page 8), TA 0-70 C, VCC +5 V +-5%: VOL 0.4 V max at IOL 1.8 mA, VOH 2.4 V min at IOH -250 uA; inputs VIL 0.8 V max, VIH 2.0 V min; clock VILC -0.3..0.45 V, VIHC VCC-0.6..VCC+0.3 V; ICC 90 mA typ, 200 mA max; input leakage 10 uA; capacitance clock 35 pF, input 5 pF, output 10 pF. Absolute maximum: any pin -0.3..+7 V, 1.5 W.

unknown: The order of the multiplexed T-state events is given by the timing waveforms on page 3 only; a cycle-exact description of every instruction (number of T states, flag results) is in the Z80 CPU technical manual, which was not read for this file.
Whether HALT, M1, RFSH and BUSAK are three-state: the pin description says 'Output, active low' without 'tri-state', so they are stored as totem-pole; the sheet does not say they float.
How NMI is detected (edge or level) is not stated on this sheet; only 'always recognized at the end of the current instruction' and the minimum low pulse of 80 ns.
notes: Card 3207 position 20F. The sheet describes both Z80-CPU (2.5 MHz) and Z80A-CPU (4 MHz); only the Z80A figures are used.

behaviour.reason: A microprocessor: its outputs depend on the program in memory and on 158 instructions with per-cycle timing that this product sheet only summarises (instruction table pages 4-5, waveforms page 3). A runnable model is a full CPU emulator, not a set of pin formulas, and the cycle-by-cycle behaviour of each instruction is not on the pages read. The words are in pins[].text, functions and state.
